body.objective: Students will be able to use ser for identity and traits.
body.iCan: I can use ser for identity and traits.
successCriteria: I can use ser for identity, origin and characteristics
I can use estar for location and temporary states
I can describe myself and others with the correct verb
body.hook: Spanish has two verbs for "to be": ser and estar. "Soy aburrido" means "I'm boring," but "Estoy aburrido" means "I'm bored." Choosing the right one changes your meaning completely, so it's worth getting right.

vocabulary.definition: To be (identity, origin, characteristics, time, profession).

study.title: ¿Ser o estar?
study.question: When do I use ser and when estar?
study.passage:
Ser: soy, eres, es, somos, sois, son. Use for:
• Identity and profession: Soy estudiante. Mi madre es enfermera.
• Origin and nationality: Soy de Edmonton. Somos canadienses.
• Characteristics: Mi hermano es alto y simpático.
• Time and dates: Son las tres. Hoy es lunes.
Estar: estoy, estás, está, estamos, estáis, están. Use for:
• Location: Estoy en la biblioteca. Calgary está en Alberta.
• Feelings and temporary states: Estoy cansada. Estamos contentos.
Meaning changes: ser aburrido (boring) / estar aburrido (bored); ser listo (clever) / estar listo (ready).
Dialogue:
Camila: ¡Hola! Soy Camila. Soy de Colombia, pero ahora vivo en Edmonton.
Andrés: Mucho gusto. Yo soy Andrés. Soy de aquí. ¿Cómo estás?
Camila: Estoy un poco nerviosa. Es mi primer día en esta escuela.
Andrés: No te preocupes. Los estudiantes son simpáticos. ¿Dónde está tu clase de matemáticas?
Camila: Está en el segundo piso.
Andrés: ¡Yo también estoy en esa clase! Vamos juntos.
English support: ahora = now; de aquí = from here; No te preocupes = don't worry; el segundo piso = the second floor; juntos = together.
Activity: Write a self-portrait in Spanish (identity, origin, personality, where you are now and how you feel today) and present it to a small group.
study.source: Original dialogue written for this lesson.
steps: Sort uses of ser and estar
Read the dialogue with a partner
discussion: Why does Camila say "Soy de Colombia" but "Estoy un poco nerviosa"?
Why is it "Está en el segundo piso"?
What is the difference between "es aburrido" and "está aburrido"?
Which uses of ser and estar appear in your self-portrait?
study.product: Write a self-portrait (8–10 sentences) using ser at least four times and estar at least three times, and explain the reason for each choice in English.

examples.title: Origin

examples.problem: Say "The library is on the first floor."
examples.answer: La biblioteca está en el primer piso.

examples.title: Meaning change
examples.problem: What's the difference between "Eres listo" and "Estás listo"?

practice.q: Which verb is used for origin?
Which verb is used for location?
Why is "Calgary está en Alberta" correct?
practice.a: Location uses estar, even for permanent places.

practice.q: Why does Andrés say "estoy en esa clase"?

misconceptions: Using estar for origin or nationality
Thinking estar is only for temporary things (location of permanent places still uses estar)
exitTicket: Write one sentence with ser and one with estar.
Explain why each verb is used.
